subject: Legend when plotting 2 data frames in one plot

messages.author: 063479fa62e3d3ae
messages.subject: Legend when plotting 2 data frames in one plot
parts:
Hi all,

I have plotted trial_prod.png and trial_cons.png exactly as I would like them to be, legend included.  I am now putting these together in one plot to create a single plot - trial.png.  I am very pleased with this - except for the legend. The legend is sorted alphabetically which is not the my preferred order (the same order as the colour layers from top to bottom).  I have tried different ways of trying to manually set the legend but all I have found so far works when plotting a single data frame and not two as I am.

It seems that using scale_colour_manual does not affect this type of plot, is there another way of doing this? 

Below is a very simple working example that also gives the same behaviour described above.

data1 = data.frame(x = seq(0,20), y = c(1,4,-5,-9,-4,0,3,6,-4,3,-2,-5,8,2,1,6,7,-9,8,-4,0))
data2 = data.frame(x = seq(0,20), y = seq(0,20))

q = ggplot(NULL, aes(x = x, y = y))
q = q + geom_line(data = data1)
q = q + geom_line(data = data2)

Thanks,
Jane

On Thu, Feb 14, 2013 at 8:59 AM, Jane <janeco...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,

> I have plotted trial_prod.png and trial_cons.png exactly as I would like
> them to be, legend included. I am now putting these together in one plot to
> create a single plot - trial.png. I am very pleased with this - except for
> the legend. The legend is sorted alphabetically which is not the my
> preferred order (the same order as the colour layers from top to bottom). I
> have tried different ways of trying to manually set the legend but all I
> have found so far works when plotting a single data frame and not two as I
> am.

It's not crystal clear what you're after, but I'll guess that you want
to combine the factor levels from two or more data frames to put into
a single legend. Your example doesn't indicate that, but let's deal
with the example first.

Is this what you're after?

library(ggplot2)

data1 = data.frame(x = seq(0,20), y =
c(1,4,-5,-9,-4,0,3,6,-4,3,-2,-5,8,2,1,6,7,-9,8,-4,0))
data2 = data.frame(x = seq(0,20), y = seq(0,20))

q = ggplot(NULL, aes(x = x, y = y))
q = q + geom_line(data = data1)

q + geom_line(data = data2)

# My guess as to what you wanted...

# row concatenate the two data frames since they have
# the same variable names
dat <- rbind(data1, data2)

# Create a factor to distinguish the data sets
dat$set <- factor(rep(c("ds1", "ds2"), times = c(nrow(data1), nrow(data2))))

# Plot the lines
ggplot(dat, aes(x = x, y = y, color = set)) + geom_line(size = 1)

I'm guessing that perhaps you want to combine two or more data frames
with the same variables, but one or more may be factors with different
sets of levels. If this is the case, redefine the factor(s) in the new
data frame with levels defined in the order you want in the legend.

If this is off base (and it may well be...notice my repeated use of
the word 'guess'), please be a bit more precise about the actual
nature of the problem with reproducible code/data to trigger it.

BTW, pre-processing data before passing it to ggplot2 is a common and
often desirable thing.. The plyr and reshape2 packages were written in
part to provide a way of pre-processing or reshaping data into a more
convenient form for input into ggplot2. It is often the case that a
few simple actions with respect to the input data can greatly simplify
the ggplot() code while producing a richer and more informative
graphic.

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Legend when plotting 2 data frames in one plot
parts:
Hi,

The plots I made use different geom_area and geom_line positions; i.e.
for the trial_prod.png plot I used:

geom_area(data = prod.data, position = "identity", alpha = 0.8)
geom_line(data = prod.data, position = "identity")

whereas for the trial_cons.png I used:

geom_area(data = cons.data, position = "stack", alpha = 0.8)
geom_line(data = cons.data, position = "stack")

Combining these in one plot gave the trial.png plot which is great
except that the legend is beyond my control. I have tried using one
data frame and setting the order of the factor and using the following:

geom_area(position = "stack", alpha = 0.8)
geom_line(position = "stack")

This produces stacked_trial.png in which the legend as set in the factor
but the plot is then not as I want it. Any tips on how to achieve my
required plot is hugely appreciated due to my quantum mechanics
flashbacks :-)

Jane
